name: Apple Computer, Inc.
summary: Founded in Cupertino, California in 1976; brought personal computing into homes, schools, and small businesses through the Apple II family and its successors.

name: International Business Machines (IBM)
summary: A dominant force in business computing from punch-card tabulating equipment through mainframes, minicomputers, and the IBM PC that defined an industry standard.

name: Digital Equipment Corporation (DEC)
summary: Founded in Maynard, Massachusetts in 1957; DEC's PDP and VAX lines pioneered minicomputing and brought interactive computing out of the glass-walled data center.

name: Commodore Business Machines
summary: Manufacturer of the best-selling Commodore 64 and the PET and Amiga lines, key to home computing's growth in the 1980s.

name: Tandy / RadioShack
summary: Retailer and manufacturer whose TRS-80 line put an affordable, complete computer on shelves in ordinary shopping malls starting in 1977.

name: Texas Instruments
summary: Electronics manufacturer known for the TI-99/4A home computer and a long line of calculators used in classrooms nationwide.

name: Atari, Inc.
summary: Pioneer of the video game industry whose 2600 console and 8-bit computers brought interactive entertainment into millions of living rooms.

name: Sinclair Research
summary: British electronics company whose inexpensive ZX-series computers introduced millions of first-time users, especially in the UK and Europe, to home computing.
